s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic, painless, periocular swelling with granulomatous inflammation
salient_findings: Painless, firm area of induration and mild erythema below the left lower eyelid
Granulomatous inflammation with central necrobiosis on histopathology
Soft-tissue thickening of the anterior-inferior orbital rim and lower eyelid on CT scan
key_facts: 69-year-old woman
Several-month history of a painless, firm area of induration and mild erythema
History of chronic scleritis treated with NSAIDs
Left levator resection for ptosis
Dacryocystorhinostomy one month before the onset of the lesion
Mass persisted despite two courses of antibiotics
Nodule remained stable in size three months after surgery
Focal, non-tender, indurated elevation along the inferior orbital rim on examination
CT scan showed soft-tissue thickening without extension into surrounding structures or bony invasion
Excisional biopsy performed
Intraoperative frozen sections revealed granulomatous inflammation
Final histopathology showed granulomatous inflammation with central necrobiosis and extensive Alcian-Blue positive mucin
No evidence of malignancy on histopathology
Bacterial and fungal stains (Ziehl–Neelsen and Grocott) were negative
